val.where: iVUE → Agreement + Account columns. The working agreement number on the service order.
val.note: Agreement types by prefix: bare NXX XXXX = phone, 101 NXX XXXX = internet, 125 001 XXXX = EDGE. Trailing IN / OUT / QDS marks the direction. iVUE export cols: Agreement, Account. Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893.

val.where: GET from LinePacks → MGCP endpoint name. PUT in iVUE → Switch Equipment column (or New Switch Equipment on reassignment). Same value as CSX/CRV/GR303 — different protocol names for the same switch-equipment box.
val.note: MGCP is the Taqua protocol flavor. Format: FRNT-PRSV_GPON-CLX01-01-04-1421-01. If not populated in iVUE, look it up in LinePacks and update Switch Equipment in iVUE. iVUE export cols: Switch Equipment, New Switch Equipment.

val.where: GET from LinePacks → GR303 endpoint name. PUT in iVUE → Switch Equipment column. Same value as CSX/MGCP — different protocol names for the same switch-equipment box.
val.note: GR303 is the Taqua protocol flavor (alternate to MGCP). If not populated in iVUE, look it up in LinePacks and update Switch Equipment in iVUE. iVUE export cols: Switch Equipment, New Switch Equipment.

val.where: GET from LinePacks → Equipment, second column. PUT in iVUE → Equipment + Equip Desc columns. The cabinet + card/slot/port identifier.
val.note: LinePacks is the source; iVUE Equipment col holds the short name (e.g. ADT-N30-1-01), Equip Desc holds the cabinet prefix (e.g. ACRN-ADT). iVUE export cols: Equipment, Equip Desc.

val.where: GET from LinePacks → Splitter view. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name on 32X SPLITTER records. Identifies the PON splitter shelf and port the customer rides.
val.note: S = splitter number, P = port number. LinePacks is the working source; iVUE export shows splitter records under Equip Type "32X SPLITTER" (e.g. MLTN-E1, MLTN-S1). iVUE export cols: Equipment Name (on SPLITTER type records).

val.where: GET from iVUE → Cable Name column OR from Fiberbook (G:\GIS_Projects). On new installs, Fiberbook/as-built may have it before iVUE. On existing service, iVUE is populated.
val.note: Cable identifier (e.g. ABRY-ACRN, BGCK-1). Pair number in adjacent Pair column. Cable Type column shows Copper/Fiber/Hybrid. iVUE export cols: Cable Name, Pair, Cable Type.

val.where: GET from Fiberbook (G:\GIS_Projects) or as-built drawings. Also in iVUE → Serving Ped Parent Equip Name column. On new fiber installs, Fiberbook/as-built is the source. On existing service, iVUE has it.
val.note: MST = Multi-Service Terminal (fiber tail), PED = Pedestal (copper/hybrid housing). iVUE export: Serving Ped Parent Equip Name (e.g. ACRN-109-5), Serv Ped Mstr Equip Cat (PED = pedestal). Cross-check Fiberbook against iVUE when they disagree.

val.where: iVUE → Serving Ped Parent Equip Name column. The pedestal or housing the home is fed from.
val.note: Format: WIRE_CENTER-ID (e.g. ACRN-109-5). This is the physical equipment feeding the premises. iVUE export cols: Serving Ped Parent Equip Name, Serv Ped Desc (short name).

val.term: Parent Equipment — Internet line item / ONT SN
val.where: GET from warehouse (new install) or Diana in Customer Care (ONT/modem assignment). PUT in iVUE → Equipment Name on ONT records (ONT-CXNK... prefix). Also in Serial column.
val.note: FSAN = the ONT serial identifier (e.g. CXNK0028C0E1). Often blank until the ONT is registered. Warehouse or Diana assigns the ONT/Modem and provides the serial. In iVUE export: Wire Center = ONT, Equipment col = the FSAN, Equip Type = Calix 711GE / 803G etc. iVUE export cols: Equipment Name (ONT-prefixed), Equipment, Serial.

sug.where: iVUE → Service Order header. The SO# identifying this order.
sug.note: Format: 6-digit number (e.g. 142965). Multiple SO#s appear when orders are bundled. In the note, written as SO# NNNNNN at the top.

sug.where: iVUE → order date. Written at the head of the note.
sug.note: Standard format: MM.DD.YY, zero-padded. Going-forward standard for automation.

sug.where: Notes → the action phrase at the top of the note after the date. Built from a controlled vocabulary of action codes.
sug.note:
Drives which workflow/variant applies. Read left to right — each code adds meaning:

DISC — Disconnect (no suffix defaults to TEL)
DISC TEL — Disconnect telephone
DISC DSL — Disconnect DSL only
DISC TEL (CBOL) — Disconnect phone, internet stays (Connected But Only-Online)
RECON — Reconnect (no suffix defaults to full service)
CONN — Connect (followed by what: QDS / speed / FTTH)
QDS — Quick Dial Service (restricted dialing rules, AKA 911-only)
VACA — Vacation (VACA DISC = leaving, VACA RECON = returning)
NPD — Non-Pay Disconnect
INT Upgrade to <speed> — Internet speed upgrade (+ BND/SNGL/ADSL/VDSL/FTTH)
CBOL — Connected But Only-Online (phone removed, internet stays)
Billing Correction — Fix billing records
Correcting Service Points — Provide 911 with line number and address

Example breakdown: DISC TEL (CBOL), QDS CONN, & Billing Correction = remove phone line (internet stays) + connect 911-only line + fix billing.

sug.where: iVUE → FACS subsystem. After edits, record whether port/pair records were touched. Use one of the standard values — do not append tech initials or context.
sug.note: Standard values: No FACS Changed / FACS Updated / FACS Removed / FACS Corrected / No FACS Listed / FACS Reverted / FACS Pending. Bonding issues and context notes go in the note body, not here.

sug.where: iVUE → Agreement column. The phone agreement being disconnected or removed. The outgoing agreement on any DISC, QDS, NPD, or MOVE order.
sug.note: Format: NXX XXXX (no area code). Agreement types: bare = phone, 101 = internet, 125 = EDGE. 559 is the area code (omit going forward). Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893. iVUE export col: Agreement.

sug.where: iVUE → Agreement column. The phone agreement being connected or added. The incoming agreement on any CONN, RECON, MOVE, or new-service order.
sug.note: Format: NXX XXXX (no area code). Agreement types: bare = phone, 101 = internet, 125 = EDGE. 559 is the area code (omit going forward). Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893. iVUE export col: Agreement.

sug.where: iVUE → Agreement column. The phone agreement for the QDS (911-only) line. A new phone agreement assigned when connecting QDS — different number from the TEL being removed (OUT).
sug.note: Format: NXX XXXX (no area code). In the note: NXX XXXX QDS IN. Agreement types: bare = phone, 101 = internet, 125 = EDGE. Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893. iVUE export col: Agreement.

sug.where: iVUE → Account column. The internet/EDGE agreement being disconnected or removed.
sug.note: Format: 101 NXX XXXX (internet) or 125 001 XXXX (EDGE). Agreement types: bare = phone, 101 = internet, 125 = EDGE. Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893. iVUE export col: Account.

sug.where: iVUE → Account column. The internet/EDGE agreement being connected or staying.
sug.note: Format: 101 NXX XXXX (internet) or 125 001 XXXX (EDGE). In the note often "101 NXX XXXX Stays". Agreement types: bare = phone, 101 = internet, 125 = EDGE. Exchanges: 822, 841, 855, 868, 877, 893. iVUE export col: Account.

sug.where: Notes → the tech signature. On its own line at the very end of the note.
sug.note: Standard format: -XX- (dash-initials-dash), own line. Known: -CT-, -JF-, -KM-. Each tech's initials also map to their writing style.

sug.where: GET from LinePacks → voice port string under *TEL section. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port columns. LinePacks is the provisioning source; iVUE holds the service record.
sug.note: Three formats: FRNT-NNNN-NNNN (copper, 75%), FRNT-xxx-ADTnn (ADSL terminal, 13%), FRNT-xxx-CLXnn (GPON/fiber, 11%). Followed on next line by TEL Location. iVUE export cols: Equipment Name (full), Port (short), Port Status.

sug.where: GET from LinePacks → data port string under *DSL section, first column (Equipment). Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port columns.
sug.note: Same formats as TEL Port. First token after *DSL in the note. iVUE export cols: Equipment Name (full), Port (short), Port Status.

sug.where: GET from LinePacks → the first bonded leg, labeled "Leg 1" in the note. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port columns. On moves/QDS, the OUT/old leg also appears here.
sug.note: Bonded service uses two legs (Leg 1 + Leg 2). Each leg has a port line then a location line, same structure as TEL/DSL. iVUE export cols: Equipment Name, Port.

sug.where: GET from LinePacks → the second bonded leg, labeled "Leg 2" in the note. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port columns.
sug.note: Bonded service uses two legs. Leg 2 in the note. iVUE export cols: Equipment Name, Port.

sug.where: GET from iVUE → FACS subsystem (cable/pair + binding-post location for the TEL port). Also visible in iVUE → Serving Ped Parent Equip Name + Serv Ped Desc columns.
sug.note: BP = binding post. The line after the TEL port in the note. iVUE export cols: Serving Ped Parent Equip Name, Serv Ped Port, Serv Ped Desc.

sug.where: GET from iVUE → FACS subsystem (cable/pair + binding-post location for the DSL port). Also visible in iVUE → Serving Ped Parent Equip Name + Serv Ped Desc columns.
sug.note: BP = binding post. The line after the DSL port in the note. iVUE export cols: Serving Ped Parent Equip Name, Serv Ped Port, Serv Ped Desc.

sug.where: Notes → the field-splicing instruction block (PIC extend / spliced-through call-outs). References cable/pair from iVUE Cable Name + Pair columns and Fiberbook.
sug.note: Flag for the splicer. Review against Fiberbook. Not stored as a field in iVUE — lives only in the note text.

sug.where: EDGE system → the EDGE (fiber) agreement. Also in iVUE → Account column with 125 prefix.
sug.note: Format: 125 001 XXXX. Agreement types: bare = phone, 101 = internet, 125 = EDGE. iVUE export col: Account (125-prefixed records).

sug.where: GET from LinePacks → switch-equipment (CRV) box. PUT in iVUE → Switch Equipment column. Same value as MGCP/GR303 — different names for the same switch-equipment box.
sug.note: Sometimes appears short (e.g. 328-1345). If not in iVUE, look it up in LinePacks and update. iVUE export cols: Switch Equipment, New Switch Equipment.

sug.where: GET from LinePacks → GPON upstream port. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name + Port on GPON equip type records.
sug.note: FTTH only. Format: WLDF-ADT-N52-1-14-GPON-B-1. iVUE export: Equip Type = GPON, Equipment Name = full string, Port = GPON-B-1.

sug.where: EDGE system → the FTTH downstream port + pair. Also in iVUE → Equipment Name on EDGE records.
sug.note: EDGE product only; rare. Format: EDGE-MLTN-FTTH PORT-D-30 PAIR 30.

sug.where: Notes metadata → which monthly file the note came from.
sug.note: "... Line Assignments" = a Service Order; "... Tech Calls" = a trouble/tech-call note. Not stored in iVUE — metadata from the source document.

sug.where: Derived from the action phrase → the classified workflow pattern.
sug.note: Big buckets: DISC_QDS_RECON, VACA_RECONNECT, DISCONNECT_ONLY, UPGRADE_*, NPD. Not a field in iVUE — derived from the action code combination.

sug.where: Notes → the "Per <name>" tag on tech-call notes, crediting who directed the field change.
sug.example: Per Bart, wound up using pr 1613 on cable 2
sug.note: Frequent names: SE, Han, Kong, Tammie. Marks a same-SO correction, not a new order. Not stored in iVUE — lives only in the note text.

sug.where: Notes + FACS → tech-call language showing the originally-assigned port was changed in the field. The corrected port then updates iVUE → Switch Equipment and FACS records.
sug.note: Signals BAD_PORT_UPDATE: the SO port did not work, FACS was updated to the real one. iVUE and LinePacks can disagree — techs note e.g. "marked bad in LinePacks but not in iVUE".

iVUE → Trouble Ticket system. The unique ticket identifier.
sug.note: Format: 6-digit number. iVUE export col: Ticket Number.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket type classification.
sug.note: Values: Service Point (92%), Locate (8%), Cable Cut, Equipment Outage, Maintenance, Out of Network. iVUE export col: Ticket Type.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket. What the customer reported when calling in.
sug.note: Controlled vocabulary. Top: NO DIAL TONE (26%), ADSL TROUBLE (22%), NOISEY/STATIC/HUM (6%), CAN'T BE CALLED (5%), NO DSL (4%), INTERNET TROUBLE/ALL (3%), NDT/NO DSL All Services Out (3%), CAN'T CALL OUT (3%). 60 distinct values. iVUE export col: Subscriber Report.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket. What was actually found to be wrong (assigned by tech after investigation).
sug.note: Controlled vocabulary. Top: CUSTOMER OWNED EQUIPMENT (17%), CENTRAL OFFICE EQUIPMENT (17%), NO TROUBLE FOUND (14%), BAD MODEM (6%), PROTECTOR/SNI/MODULE (5%), BURIED CABLE (4%), PAIR (1.5%), INSIDE WIRING (1.3%), CUT CABLE (1%), PEDESTAL (1%). 103 distinct values. iVUE export col: Fault.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket. Root cause of the trouble (why the fault happened).
sug.note: Controlled vocabulary. Mirrors Fault values closely. Top: CUSTOMER OWNED EQUIPMENT (17%), CENTRAL OFFICE EQUIPMENT (16%), NO TROUBLE FOUND (13%), BAD MODEM (6%), PROTECTOR/SNI/MODULE (4%), BURIED CABLE/DROP (3%), PAIR (2%), INSIDE WIRING (1.5%). 103 distinct values. iVUE export col: Cause.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket. How the ticket was resolved.
sug.note: Controlled vocabulary. Values: REPAIRED (56%), NO ACTION TAKEN (22%), OTHER (12%), LOCATE DONE (8%), TEMPORARY FIX (1%), CANCELLED (<1%). iVUE export col: Resolution.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket. Plant disposition — where the trouble was and what type of visit.
sug.note: Controlled vocabulary. Top: TROUBLE INSIDE CO/RT (18%), CPE - PREM VISIT (9%), CABLE/PROT/DROP-NO PREM V (9%), DSL/COE-PREM VISIT (7%), NO TROUBLE FOUND (6%), CUSTOMER IW/EQUIPMENT (5%). 35 distinct values. iVUE export col: Plant.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket. Broader plant classification category.
sug.note: Groups Plant values into categories. Top: TROUBLE INSIDE CO/RT (18%), CPE - PREMISE VISIT (9%), CABLE/PROT/DROP (9%), BROADBAND - PREM VISIT (7%), NO TROUBLE FOUND (6%). 34 distinct values. iVUE export col: Plant Category.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket. The action taken to resolve.
sug.note: Sparse field (only 135 populated). Values: Replaced Equip, CUSTOMER, Repaired Existing, AUTHORITIES, No action needed, Customer Education, Reset/Reprogrammed. iVUE export col: Action.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket. Free-text notes on how the ticket was resolved.
sug.note: Free text field. The tech narrative equivalent of the SO note body. iVUE export col: Resolve Notes.

sug.where: iVUE → Trouble Ticket. Additional remarks about the trouble.
sug.note: Free text field. May contain field tech observations, customer context, history. iVUE export col: Trouble Remarks.
